file.content:
import pytest

from stats import mean, median


def test_mean():
    assert mean([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2.5


def test_median_odd():
    assert median([3, 1, 2]) == 2


def test_median_even():
    # With an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle
    # values, not the upper one.
    assert median([1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2.5


def test_median_does_not_mutate():
    values = [3, 1, 2]
    median(values)
    assert values == [3, 1, 2]

All 4 tests pass.

The bug was in `median()` in `stats.py`: for even-length input it returned the upper-middle element (`ordered[len//2]`) instead of the mean of the two middle values. Fixed by averaging the two central elements when the length is even. No test files were changed.
